column1: # cyanrip fork fatal/error message inventory — 128 strings, handshake round 12.
# PROVENANCE, so a reader can re-derive it rather than trust it:
#   PROVIDER-CONTRACT.md, section "P5 - Fatal and error message inventory"
#   source anchor sha256/16 = f606f536c72da8cc  over src/*.c and src/*.h
# DERIVED FROM CONTROL FLOW on the fork's side, with every `goto <label>`
# DISCOVERED from the source rather than enumerated. The history is the point:
#    88 — filtered through a hand-maintained 21-word prefix allowlist (round 4)
#   104 — control flow, but with a hand-maintained list of goto LABELS (round 5)
#   115 — labels discovered from source, so an unforeseen one cannot vanish (round 6)
#   130 — round 9 lap 3, which finally scanned `genopt.h` (see below)
#   128 — round 12; two rows left `cyanrip_log()` and so left their generator's
#         population. They did NOT stop being printed — see RETAINED_BEYOND_P5 in
# Twice the same defect one level up: a hand-maintained list replacing a
# hand-maintained list and being called derived.
# THIS FILE WAS STUCK AT ROUND 6's 115 FOR FIVE ROUNDS. Round 8 lap 1 §D2 told us
# in prose ("the contract grew by 10 fatal messages, and the program did not");
# round 9 lap 3 attached the table itself, and it is committed in this repo at
# Two of those ten genopt strings matched NOTHING in our surfacing pattern:
#   genopt.h:564  Programming error, incorrect type for: %s
#   genopt.h:598  Too many values for argument "%s" (at most %i)
# so either one rendered to the user as a bare "Rip failed." The other eight
# survived only on the word-prefix fallback, which is forward tolerance, not
# coverage. It went unnoticed because the test comparing this file against the
# in-code inventory compared two expressions of the SAME round — consistent, and
# not verified. The staleness check that closes that hole is
# Our surfacing pattern is built FROM this inventory
# (src/platterpus/ripper_messages.py), not from a prefix guess of our own —
# because when both sides guess, both guess alike, and our 90/90 test was green
# The evidence column matters and is preserved in
# src/platterpus/ripper_message_inventory.py: 84 rows are proven reachable on a
# failure path without reference to wording; the other 44 rest on weaker grounds
# and must not be treated as hard fatals.
# Do not hand-edit. Replaced wholesale when a round ships a new inventory; a diff
# here is a change in what the ripper can say to us.
